newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet says customer base reviving.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet says customer base reviving.

text.p: ValuJet Inc chairman Lewis Jordan, speaking a year after a plane crash that killed all 100 people aboard, said load factors were improving and the airline was rebuilding its customer base.
"We are not 100 percent satisfied with the total revenue picture, but our cash reserves are still the strongest among any of the small carriers," Jordan told CNN in an interview aired on Sunday.
"We have lot of staying power and the customer base is building. We are getting good support from the travelling public," he said.
ValuJet's Atlanta-bound Flight 592 crashed into the Florida Everglades on May 11, 1996.
Press reports say the National Transportation Safety Board will criticise the airline and the Federal Aviation Administration when it issues a final report in July.
ValuJet maintains that no decision or action by the airline or its employees can be linked to the accident.
Jordan underscored the airline's commitment to safety and said it had always been a priority.

He said his priority now was to achieve "operational excellence," adding that "measured growth, conservative growth at this time, is more appropriate under the circumstances" than any decisions to expand the airline's routes or services.
Jordan said the airline's load factors were rising and approaching year-earlier levels.
ValuJet lost $41.5 million in 1996, including a $68 million charge taken to reflect its grounding after the fatal crash.
